title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on 'groupes de Galois motiviques, cas commutatif, corps de base fini'. The page is a sketch of the Tannakian structure of the category M of motives over k = F_p.

(1) Realizations. For each prime l ≠ p, l-adic cohomology gives a fibre functor T_l: M → Mod(Ẑ, Q_l). This is the category of Q_l-representations of Gal(k̄/k) ≅ Ẑ, i.e. the étale realization with its geometric Frobenius action. For l = p, crystalline cohomology gives a functor to F-(iso)crystals over W(F_p)[1/p] = Q_p. Since σ is trivial on W(F_p) = Z_p, Frobenius is Q_p-linear. So an F-isocrystal over F_p is just a Q_p-vector space with an automorphism, an object of Mod(Z, Q_p). Grothendieck stresses that Z cannot be replaced by Ẑ here. The Frobenius eigenvalues have nonzero p-adic valuations (slopes), so the Z-action does not extend continuously to Ẑ. This is the p-adic asymmetry between the l-adic and crystalline realizations.

(2) Artin(–Tate) part. Niv^0(M) is the subcategory of motives of level ('niveau') 0. Niv^0(M)^0 is a further subcategory; the underlined phrase defining it is illegible. Since the text then sets F^0(Q(1)) = Q, Niv^0(M)^0 is presumably the ⊗-subcategory generated by Artin motives (H^*(X) for X finite étale over k) and Tate twists, i.e. Artin–Tate motives. On it there is a natural rational fibre functor F^0: Niv^0(M)^0 → Mod(Q, π), with π = π_1(k) = Ẑ. Its targets are Q-vector spaces with Galois action, i.e. locally constant étale sheaves of Q-vector spaces on Spec k. It is defined by F^0(H^*(X)) = f_*(Q_X) for f: X → Spec k finite, and F^0(Q(1)) = Q. (The arrow is first written to Mod(Q, Ẑ), corrected to Mod(Q, π).)

(3) Sub-gerbe. Inside the gerbe of ⊗-fibre functors of M, one considers the sub-gerbe of fibre functors extending F^0. Its band is the commutative group Ker(G^0 →ε G_m). Here G^0 is presumably the identity component / Weil-number part of the motivic group, and ε is the weight (Tate) character. So the motivic gerbe over F_p is reduced, relative to the explicitly known Artin–Tate part, to a gerbe with commutative band.

(4) Under the Tate conjecture and Honda–Tate, G is identified as the group of multiplicative type over Q whose character group is the group of Weil numbers. This is the 'Weil-number protorus'.

Purpose: describe the (non-neutral) motivic Galois gerbe over a finite field explicitly, as an extension of the Artin–Tate part by a protorus determined by Weil numbers.
errors: Not an error but a gap: it is not stated whether the sub-gerbe of fibre functors extending F^0 is nonempty over Q. In fact Mot(F_p) has no Q-valued (even R-valued) fibre functor. For example, the endomorphism algebra of a supersingular elliptic curve is the quaternion algebra ramified at p and ∞. So this sub-gerbe is a non-neutral gerbe over Q. The fragmentary text does not make this explicit, but may well have intended it.

The crystalline realization is described as landing in F-crystals 'over Q_p'. Strictly these are F-isocrystals over W(F_p)[1/p]. The identification with (Q_p-vector space, automorphism) is correct only because the base is the prime field F_p (σ = id). Over F_q with q = p^a, one gets σ-semilinear Frobenius and must use its a-th power.
'Tate-Honda' is listed among the 'conjectures'. Honda–Tate is a theorem (Tate 1966/68, Honda 1968); only the Tate conjecture is conjectural here.

ideas.what: Family of realization functors on motives over F_p: l-adic into Q_l-representations of Ẑ, crystalline into Q_p-spaces with a Z-action (automorphism) that does not extend to Ẑ
ideas.modern_name: l-adic and crystalline realizations; Frobenius slopes; Weil-group vs Galois-group realizations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (motives, crystalline cohomology, 1960s), Berthelot (crystalline cohomology 1974); the realization-system viewpoint in Saavedra Rivano 1972, Deligne–Milne 1982
ideas.where_published: Ideas present in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) and motive discussions; the precise Mod(Z,Q_p) vs Mod(Ẑ,Q_l) remark not known to me in print by him

ideas.what: Rational fibre functor on Artin–Tate motives over a finite field: F^0(h(X)) = f_*Q_X, F^0(Q(1)) = Q
ideas.modern_name: Q-valued fibre functor on Artin–Tate motives over F_q; the Artin–Tate subcategory is neutral
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972); Milne, 'Motives over finite fields' (1994)

ideas.what: Sub-gerbe of fibre functors on Mot(F_p) extending a given fibre functor on the Artin–Tate part, banded by the kernel of the weight character on the connected motivic group
ideas.modern_name: Motivic gerbe over F_q as extension of the Artin–Tate gerbe by the Weil-number protorus; Langlands–Rapoport pseudomotivic groupoid

ideas.what: Under the Tate conjecture and Honda–Tate, the (connected) motivic group over F_p is the group of multiplicative type over Q with character group the Weil numbers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano 1972 (attributing ideas to Grothendieck/Deligne), Milne 1994, Langlands–Rapoport 1987

missed.claim: Documentary evidence that Grothendieck himself sketched the structure of the motivic Galois gerbe over F_p. This includes the Weil-number protorus via Tate and Honda–Tate, and its relation to a canonical Q-fibre functor on the Artin–Tate part. The literature usually presents this via Saavedra, Deligne–Milne and Milne. The content is now standard, so this is attribution/history rather than new mathematics.
missed.quote: Dans le groupe des foncteurs fibres de M ... prolongeant F^0 ... Ker(G^0 →ε G_m) ... Par ailleurs, ... conj. de Tate et de Tate-Honda, G est le groupe ... sur Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Clarifies the provenance of the Weil-number-torus description of Mot(F_q) and of the Langlands–Rapoport-style splitting relative to Artin–Tate motives. It also shows the explicit remark that the crystalline realization only has a Z-action (Weil group), not a Ẑ-action.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is the now-standard description of motives over finite fields: realizations, the Artin–Tate neutral part, and the Weil-number protorus under Tate and Honda–Tate. It is fully developed in Saavedra, Deligne–Milne, Langlands–Rapoport and Milne. The only modest interest is historical: an early Grothendieck sketch, including the sub-gerbe of fibre functors extending F^0 on Artin–Tate motives.
transcription_corrections: 'Mod(Q, Ẑ)' is crossed out after F^0 and replaced by 'Mod(Q, π)' written under the arrow; the right-hand note reads roughly 'i.e. faisceaux de Q-vect. [loc. constants] sur k'.
'Dans le groupe des foncteurs fibres' is more plausibly 'Dans la gerbe des foncteurs fibres' (a 'G' is inserted above), and 'le sous-groupe' is likely 'la sous-gerbe 𝒢_𝒦' / sub-gerbe.
'un groupe commutatif sur k' may be 'sur Q'; the context (Weil-number torus) points to Q.
'F-cristaux' is more accurately F-isocristaux (the text has 'F-cristaux sur Q_p').
The final lines likely read 'en vertu des conj. de Tate et de Tate-Honda, G est le groupe de type multiplicatif sur Q, dual du groupe des caractères [nombres de Weil]'.
The left marginal note beside the bracket ('un des pour lequel?') is illegible and not transcribed.
